en: The Praise Entitled *Guṇasragdharā* to the Blessed One, the Glorious Hevajra, by the Great Paṇḍita Śrī Śūnyasamādhivajrapāda.
Homage to the Glorious Hevajra!
Even the Lord of the Nāgas in Pātāla, though possessing power equal to the minister of the Lord of Heaven, is not able to praise Your glory because of his own limitations;
nor is the wise mortal in the world of men capable enough to fully proclaim Your true virtues, despite his many enjoyments.
Nevertheless, I shall today utter a hymn of praise, though deficient in eloquence, yet joined with devotion and reasoned application. ||1||

The Buddhas, the sons of the Perfectly Awakened Ones, those holding the supreme vajra in their hands, the Śrāvakas, the Pratyekabuddhas, the gods, Gandharvas, Siddhas, Uragas, Māyās, Munis, Yakṣas, Rākṣasas, and Asuras— having praised you, who possess the power of the Ten Powers, according to their own respective capacities, they worship you perfectly.
Indeed, even one who possesses merit is worthy of honor in this world; how much more so one like you, a teacher of all! (2)
Brahmā and the others, who were blinded by pride and deprived of their own power, upon beholding Your majesty,

have their ears filled with the sound of *hūṃ*, their mental faculties dulled and agitated, and being tormented by fear, they fall bewildered at the soles of Your feet as You dance with the nine aesthetic sentiments.
O Protector, those whose thoughts are not stilled would suffer great humiliation for failing to understand this. //3//
Having cast aside your most precious form, which captivates the eyes of living beings and is marked by auspicious characteristics upon its limbs,
you assume a terrifying, fierce form that strikes fear into the wicked.
This is the practice of celibacy (*brahmacarya*) within the mandala, manifested as the singular nature of wisdom and skillful means.
O Vajrin, by means of conduct and non-conduct, even that which is accumulated is quickly revealed by that Āryā. 4.
With the mirror of knowledge, you behold phenomena—obscured, concealed, and far-reaching;
this is that Vairocana, whose true nature is the form of a Buddha, devoted to the welfare of self and others.
Through the wisdom of equality, you perceive the Buddhas in every direction as being of undifferentiated form.
May he, who dwells within your body, speech, and mind as the King of Jewels, Śrī, and who appears in the form of an enemy, protect you. ||5||
I discern with equanimity, for even a single moment, all those phenomena that exist— however many there may be— in their ultimate nature as aggregates, elements, and so forth;
and that third wisdom called "discriminating awareness," which produces the welfare of the Victors.
The glorious one, whose form is that of the Lord of Speech, the abode of a multitude of virtues, and liberated from the snares of delusion. ||6||
All sentient beings— those dwelling in space, those moving through the realms of the seasons, and all those born of the four modes of birth—
who are afflicted, devoid of equal happiness, and consumed by the fire of intense suffering: for their sake,
you act daily through non-apprehension as the *he*-kāra-vajra.
The gnosis that performs its function, which benefits the beings born within the three realms, has the nature of the vajra of karma. ||7||

Knowledge that is unobstructed, pure, removing all stains and conceptual constructions, accomplishing its own purpose, radiant with brilliant power, dispelling thick darkness, noble and indestructible, joyful, personally realized, auspicious, possessing unequaled bliss, pervasive, and having the nature of the Lord of the Mind.
O Protector, by that very [means], you also constantly enter the utterly pure realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu). ||8||

Inexpressible as one or many, like the sky, its nature is eternal emptiness; it transcends the proliferation of existence and non-existence, is free from transformation, all-pervading, and accessible only to the Buddhas.
It is the cause of the attainment of true being, the generator of hundreds of virtues, and the embodiment of exquisite bliss.
Unimpeded by the lack of intrinsic nature of the body, he who accomplishes the welfare of himself and others remains present in every way. ||9||
In a pure Buddha-field composed of various jewels, upon a mountain peak, he has spread out a manifold, supramundane, and supreme sovereignty born from the power of his own accumulated merit;
he is the eternal sovereign of Dharma, a treasury of all virtues, the omniscient teacher of all.
Your enjoyment body (sāmbhogika-kāya) brings joy to all Buddhas with a rain of the sublime Dharma. 10.
Sometimes manifesting noble birth and perfect enlightenment, or sometimes performing the recollection of the wheel of the Dharma due to its utter purity;
and again, for the sake of the welfare of sentient beings, displaying his physical form;
being all-pervading, assuming every form, acting for the benefit of the three worlds, he shines forth most brilliantly as a virtuous one.
Your emanation body performs solely for the benefit of all sentient beings, like a magical illusion. ||11||
The Buddha was tightly bound with nooses resembling serpent-nooses joined with elephant-irons; with his limbs perfectly contracted, his teeth were closely pressed together like those of a tortoise;
moreover, his upper body was covered in sweat as he was thoroughly scorched by the harsh rays of the sun, just as you [were].
O Great-souled One, by grasping Your name with devotion, one becomes endowed with happiness, even when released from the hand.

Having emerged from the interior fire of the serpent, terrifying with its clearly expanded and formidable hoods, from that radiant one possessing a fierce body, who is as restless as the flickering end of the sky (or time),
bearing uneven poison, with a red face at twilight and large, rolling, red, and blazing eyes;
Even one who has lost their life from a crawling serpent on their body becomes [liberated] by being a devotee who remembers You. ||13||
Though being consumed by the blazing masses of forest fires— terrible with leaping flames, scattered with sparks from the tips of many hoods,
grey with intense, rising smoke, and roaring with the thunderous sound of supreme forces—
he, with a distressed mind, [remained] amidst those glowing conflagrations.
O treasury of virtues, the one who has faith in you attains success; liberated and with uninjured limbs, he speaks.

The path— difficult to traverse, with distant shores, filled with water as bitter as salt, garlanded with rows of tossing waves, strewn with swaying serpents, where the surface of the ocean is agitated by the blows of the trunks of great sea-monsters,
hidden by crocodiles hard to seize, white with the foam of young calves, and infested with whirlpools, sharks, and snakes— is [the way].
Sinking in the ocean of existence, one who has fallen into it reaches the further shore, freed from suffering, by counting your multitude of virtues. ||15||

With tawny and brownish-red beard, eyelashes, and eyebrows, and with a frown upon his brow; with blood-red eyes dancing in the sky, mouth wide open, tongue flickering, and hair like blazing fire; terrifying with his curved tusks, his mouth-cavity adorned by a garland of severed heads, and emitting a blood-dripping, loud, and boisterous laugh.
Even toward those who devour raw flesh, you immediately retreat from their presence, O you who are bowed by devotion.
In that furious battle— where horses were struck down by showers of various iron arrows, where blows from spears were dealt,
where armor vomited forth flames, where heads were severed by swords whetted on whetstones,
and where streams of blood flowed from the frontal globes of elephants split by discuses—
O Lord, he who is twice entwined by [the cycle of birth] is liberated from it through the recitation of your praises. ||17||
Scattering the leaves of the *pūtavallī* and crushing the tips of the trees, obstructed by the agitation of its own friction, it creates a downpour of harsh and rough stones;
causing the waters to surge and casting down the peaks of the mountains, the wind moves on.
O Lord, peace comes from your name when it is uttered together with prostration and salutation.
In a wilderness marked by thorns, rugged with harsh and stony rocks, and along a difficult path where fierce and darting flames flicker,
a hero— his slender body nourished by the consumption of sweet deer flesh—
encounters a terrifying beast of cruel fangs rushing toward him from the mouth of a cave.
For one meditating upon you, there shall be no fear; for you are the pacifier of the dread of worldly existence—what else is there in the world besides you? 19.

Having worshipped with various offerings— tawny, powerful, and most excellent— at each and every desire-fulfilling rite, those who always pay homage to the book whose words are written according to the ritual rules,
they rejoice in heaven with beautiful women, or in pleasure at the river of the gods, or at Nandana.
O Lord, the offerings duly presented day after day to one worthy of worship certainly bear fruit. ||20||

The Lord of Gods, whose lotus-feet are rubbed by the clearly visible jewel-crowns of the hosts of deities, resides in the Vaijayanta palace; his body is adorned with a weight of jewels that radiate vast beams of light.
Beholding the moon-like face of Śacī and listening well to her extensive and melodious songs, he remains there.
O Lord, who always remains intent on offering praise to Your lotus feet with devotion? ||21||

Māndhātā, the upholder of Dharma, was honored by gods, serpents, and men; likewise honored were those two protectors of the earth, whose bodies possessed strength equal to that of the world-protectors (Lokapālas), and who were surrounded by ascetics.
They were praised by bards and fanned at the tips of yak-tail whisks waved by the hands of young women.
Through the practice of worshiping the Lord, you two shone with intense delight for the supreme goal, as if possessing the sovereignty of a beautiful creeper. ||22||

Śeṣa, the lord of all serpents, whose feet are reddened by the lac-like rays of the foremost jewel upon the head of the king of snakes who serves as his couch, from whose breath fire is exhaled, whose expansion illuminates the quarters with the rays of the jewels on his hoods, and whose color is like a blue lotus in a sky filled with water-laden clouds; [I bow to him].
By your power, the earth bears the world along with its waters and the celestial river. ||23||
Those fools who, ignorant of the ultimate truth, revile you— the noble Teacher— shall at the end endure suffering born of burning, cooking, cleaving, and the like;
they shall plunge into the wretched Avīci hell, into a great wave filled with vessels of molten iron as hot as the sun.
She who swiftly dissolves the seven bodily constituents, such as the skin and others, which arise from the movement of the vital breaths.
But you have obtained your seat, which is auspicious, the state of immortality, the destroyer of the mass of sufferings,

the supreme good that effects the welfare of beings, naturally pure, difficult to attain, and worthy of worship. Fools, however, through their delusions and other faults, cling to the doctrines of the heretics, which are extremely defiled, worldly, and a source of suffering.
Surely they quickly fall into the contemptible state of animals, which is devoid of pure qualities. ||25||
Those who, being excessively greedy for your wealth— whether it be small or great— become utterly deluded by that which is terrible, sharp, like poison in its maturation, and causes intense torment,
shall become *preta*s with needle-like mouths, whose bellies are as vast as the ocean, and who utter piteous cries.
Emaciated by hunger, with sunken eyes and an exceedingly soiled throat, his neck was parched with thirst. ||26||
He who recites this seed-mantra of Vajravārāhī, which brings victory, speaks with diverse speech through prose and verse composed of graceful words;
being possessed of tranquility, he quells the arguments of the visible lords of disputants, just as a lion quells an elephant's pride.
He would be the knower of the universe; he brings forth the people from his own self and [establishes] beautiful conduct. ||27||
The wish-fulfilling tree, the cow of plenty, the sword moving through the sky, the elixir of longevity,
the eye-ornament, the auspicious jar, the treasure of taste, the pill, the beautiful jewel-lake,
the six masters of silence, the superknowledges, and the entry into the house of strength— these and others are known as the excellent qualities.
Furthermore, other efforts as well, along with their attendants, attain success through you. ||28||
The yogin named Viśvarūpa, whose speech was auspicious and whose appearance was as tranquil and sweet as honey,
by the power of yoga caused the sun, which had reached the vault of the sky, to become ninefold.

Near the Godāvarī, that which repeatedly causes a terrifying burst of effort from the host of the weak—this entire splendor of the one whose form is radiant is the playfulness of him who pervades the three worlds. 29.
O Heruka, by your grace, the most auspicious mudrā that pacifies all suffering has been attained by yogis of vast intellect— such as Ḍombī, Vajrā, Abjavajrā, and others— who are established in yoga;
whereas Caṇḍālī, with her fierce mind, devoted to the unwholesome and intent on killing, is [otherwise].
Having approached you, they reach the stainless state of tranquility, having transcended conventional rules of conduct. ||30||
The dhāraṇīs, the stages, the suns, and the tenfold commands of mastery increase for that King of Dharma, just as subjects do for a monarch;
they remain devoted, like women, always changeless and rich in virtues.
O glorious one, like a wish-fulfilling tree, all prosperities abide in you who are devoted to the welfare of others. //31//

O Lord, you constantly behold this entire world through the immeasurables such as loving-kindness; yet you do not perceive them, nor do you perceive yourself, for you possess vast being and are eternally free from conceptual parts. You bring forth the rain of the sublime Dharma for sentient beings, yet you never perceive them at any time.
That non-conceptual [wisdom], which bestows upon the worlds whatever desired wealth is wished for like a wish-fulfilling gem—[that is what is being described]. ||32||
You are my mother, you are my father, you are my great refuge; you are indeed the Lord, you are the Teacher,
and with your fresh compassion, O Protector of all living beings, you are the cutter away of all faults for me,
who am wandering in saṃsāra, pierced by the hundreds of arrows of calamity, and deprived of honor.
May this month, meritorious, pure, and bringing supreme happiness, lead to liberation through the realization of the Command. ||33||

O Lord, by whatever merit has been produced by me through this hymn of praise to You— which is uniquely capable of washing away all the impurities of the Kali age and is as radiant as jasmine and the rays of the moon—
may the Lord Heruka, the abode of glory, swiftly become the refuge for all beings within the three worlds.
He who acts for the benefit of beings with perfect correctness, a treasury of the wealth of the Guru’s qualities, is the Great King of Dharma. ||34||
This concludes the praise entitled *Guṇasragdharā* for the Blessed Lord Śrī Hevajra. This work is the composition of the great scholar, the venerable Śūnyasamādhivajrapāda.
